'''Naan''' is a round [[Cookbook:Flatbread|flatbread]] made with white [[Cookbook:Flour|flour]] and is a staple accompaniment to hot meals in central and southern Asia.

== Ingredients ==
* 3 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] (450 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) plain [[Cookbook:Flour|flour]]
* 1 cup (240 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]]) [[Cookbook:Yogurt|yogurt]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Baking Soda|baking soda]]
* 2 teaspoons [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* ¾ cup (180 ml) water

== Procedure ==
# Make the dough by [[Cookbook:Kneading|kneading]] together all the ingredients and sufficient water (this will be approximately ¾ cup but some judgement is required).
# Wrap the dough in a damp muslin cloth and leave it to rise for 2–3 hours.
# Divide the dough into small balls.
# [[Cookbook:Dough#Rolling|Roll out]] the balls in oblong or round shapes with a [[Cookbook:Rolling Pin|rolling pin]] or by slapping and stretching with your hands.
# Smear the surface with water and bake in a tandoor or preheated [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] (as hot as your oven will go).
# The naans should puff up a little, and be ready to remove from the oven in 4–5 minutes.
# [[Cookbook:Brush|Brush]] the naan with butter. Serve hot.

==Notes, tips, and variations==
* To add an extra crispy finish, pop the baked naans under a preheated grill for 30 seconds before brushing with butter and serving.
* To add extra flavour, consider adding finely-[[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]] [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]] and coriander to the butter you brush over your cooked naan breads. Then return them to the oven (or place under a grill) for a short time to cook the garlic.
